summary: This note describes the Novorossiya Governorate (New Russia Governorate), a governorate of the Russian Empire formed in previously Ottoman and Cossack territories. It existed from 1764 until an administrative reform in 1783 and was created and governed under the Russian Senate's "Plan for the Colonization of New Russia Gubernia." The note also records that it was the first Russian region where Catherine the Great allowed foreign Jews to settle.
one_line: Novorossiya Governorate was a Russian Empire governorate from 1764 to 1783 in former Ottoman and Cossack lands, notable for admitting foreign Jewish settlers.
key_facts: Novorossiya Governorate, also called New Russia Governorate, was a governorate of the Russian Empire.
The governorate was located in previously Ottoman and Cossack territories.
The Novorossiya Governorate existed from 1764 until the administrative reform of 1783.
It was created and governed according to the "Plan for the Colonization of New Russia Gubernia" issued by the Russian Senate.
Novorossiya Governorate became the first region in Russia where Catherine the Great allowed foreign Jews to settle.
The Russian name of the governorate is transliterated as "Novorossiyskaya guberniya".
